# Phase-selective retained crystal rewriting: working research record

Date: 14 October 2026.
Status: unvalidated physical hypothesis plus conditional analytical calculations.
No physical experiment, atomistic simulation, industrial advantage, or novelty
certification was obtained. This record was created in the conversation workspace;
it was not published to the Astra repository.

Repository consulted: harjassand/astra-research-knowledge, revision
`ace0cfc4437fe91c20ccd24d69e0ee4bb335e871`. Relevant negative records: N783
(retained repair and outgoing-carrier qualification) and N789 (unacquired
same-specimen coherent-recoil retained-write response). These negatives remain
unchanged; no source-unreviewed mathematical result is promoted here.

## Proposed physical operation

Use a common phase-locked fundamental/second-harmonic field to distinguish
inversion-related crystal variants and bias which variant remains after the
field is removed. The proposed output is retained polarity selection or directed
antiphase-boundary migration, not an optical signal, carrier current, heating
contrast, or mere disappearance of material.

Restrict the hypothesis to domains whose inversion relation and opposite nonlinear
response have actually been established. Not every translational antiphase domain
can simply be assigned opposite optical susceptibility. Use a geometry with a
nonzero population-control tensor projection. A (111) optical experiment cannot
supply the contrast for normally illuminated (001) material.

In a two-channel perturbative model, opposite variants can have excitation
probabilities proportional to sum_f |a_f + s exp(i phi) b_f|^2, with s=+1 or -1.
A phase shift of pi exchanges the interference contribution. This is established
coherent-control structure, not a new law discovered here. Whether it changes a
retained structural transition is the missing physical operation.

## Strong comparators and scope of novelty

Post-growth thermal antiphase-boundary removal already exists. Fabrication of
chosen orientation patterns through bonding, lithography and epitaxial regrowth
also exists. Neither APB elimination nor patterned polarity itself is claimed new.
The proposed differentiator is post-growth phase-selected correction/reconfiguration
without imposing the existing template and processing requirements, and only if a
matched whole-process comparison estab

# Phase-selective structural writing with finite retention

**Disposition.** A non-melting route is mathematically possible, but an optical population contrast does not establish one. A small phase-odd excitation can select and retain a structural polarity over a finite, specified horizon if (i) the sample has two experimentally identified symmetry-related variants, (ii) phase reversal changes the *structural transition kernel* in the corresponding odd direction, and (iii) the pulse moves an existing boundary or nucleates/grows a selected variant faster than field-free reverse transitions erase it. Detailed balance permits this during a driven pulse; removal of the drive restores symmetric kinetics; for an irreducible finite chain, long-time dynamics eventually erase ensemble polarity. The missing physical control is a measured, phase-reversible retained structural kernel under matched heat and direct-field controls, not another carrier-contrast number.

Separately, the incoming physical phase-rewriting source record (`work/FM-sources/physical/RESEARCH_RECORD.md`) derives an impulsive complete-melting contrast threshold C > 0.4484916 only under its equal-mole, fixed-composition, equilibrium complete-melting energy-partition assumptions. This conditional enthalpy calculation is not an N777 result and is not a general lower bound for structural switching. A real optical ferroelectric domain-switching experiment shows that wall-mediated structural switching can be written without melting an entire domain: in freestanding BaTiO3, 391 nm light switches an upward region downward while a measured imprint selects the downward state and photoexcitation lowers the wall-motion barrier. The paper estimates only 0.25–0.5 K heating in a COMSOL model and reports above-bandgap-only switching; it also reports optical-write/electrical-reset cycles. The cycle documents a structural write followed by reset under that protocol, but is not a controlled post-light-off retention curve over a declared hold interval. This is a useful non-bulk-melt precedent, but the direction is selected by the built-in imprint, not a coherent phase-odd selector.

This analysis is a conditional model and primary-literature audit. It does not establish a new capability, favorable material rates, novelty, cost superiority, or any transfer to GaAs, hBN, BaTiO\(_3\), Te, or another material.

# GaAs post-growth polarity rewriting: materials and process-path audit

**Date:** 15 October 2026  
**Scope:** Retained, phase-selected GaAs polarity/APB rewriting; primary process comparators and adjacent laser pathways.  
**Status:** Feasibility screen with conditional thermodynamic arithmetic. No new physical response or retained phase-selected structure was experimentally demonstrated here.

## Decision

The proposed operation is physically conceivable only if the illuminated boundary separates variants with the required opposite phase-odd response and the resulting excitation biases an irreversible boundary transition. Neither condition has been demonstrated on the proposed GaAs-on-Si material. The strongest available optical result is a roughly 2% phase-dependent **carrier-density modulation** in a different, 650 nm (111) GaAs specimen. It is not a measurement of phase-dependent deposited heat, APB mobility, or a retained polarity change.

The concrete target geometry chosen for comparison is the published on-axis 300 mm Si(001) substrate with a 400 nm GaAs film. With a 20 nm Al2O3 cap and a 650 °C, 7.5 min Ar furnace anneal, its measured surface APB line density falls from 0.10 to 0.014 μm⁻¹. That is a 86% reduction (7.14-fold) without phase selection. The remaining domains show a nonzero plateau, while depth profiles after at least 650 °C for 10 min show nearly undetectable APBs through most—but not all—of the film. This is a strong retained-material comparator.

For normally incident, co-propagating fields on a (001) zincblende surface, the direct bulk third-rank interference contraction is zero: the allowed cubic components are xyz permutations, while both fields have only in-plane x/y components. A p-polarized oblique-incidence or otherwise z-polarized geometry could avoid this tensor zero, but the local carrier and absorbed-energy contrast must be measured under the actual cap, substrate, fluence, and temperature. The proposed normal-incidence transfer from the (111) optical experiment does not qualify.

**Disposition:** Do not treat phase-selective retained APB rewriting as an available GaAs operation or build a processing architecture around it. Preserve it as a specimen-scale hypothesis whose first decisive endpoint is signed, retained boundary displacement that reverses under φ→φ+π, with structural and composition checks.
